title: Letter Combinations of a Phone Number
hints: if digits is empty, there are no combinations to build - handle that as a base case up front
recurse with an index into digits and a 'current combination so far' string or character list
at each call, look up the letters for digits[index], and for each letter, append it to the current combination, recurse on index + 1, then remove that letter before trying the next one

when index reaches the end of digits, the current combination is complete - add it to your results; since you always try letters in the keypad's natural a-b-c order, the results come out already sorted lexicographically
commonMistakes: not handling the empty-string input as a special case, which can produce a spurious single empty combination instead of no output at all
forgetting to remove the last appended character before trying the next letter, which corrupts the current combination for later branches
hardcoding the digit-to-letters mapping incorrectly (7 and 9 have 4 letters, not 3, unlike the other digits)

content.problemStatement:
You're given a string of digits from 2 to 9, using the classic phone
keypad mapping (2 = abc, 3 = def, 4 = ghi, 5 = jkl, 6 = mno, 7 = pqrs,
8 = tuv, 9 = wxyz).

**Return every letter combination that the digits could represent, as
a single space-delimited string, with the combinations sorted in
lexicographic (alphabetical) order.**

If the input is empty, return an empty string.
constraints: digits[i] is a digit in the range ['2', '9']
notes: empty input string (output is an empty string)
a single digit (no cross product needed)
digits mapping to keys with different letter counts, e.g. 7 and 9 which have 4 letters each versus keys with 3

optimal.pattern: backtracking, building one combination character by character and undoing the last character before trying the next

bruteForce.approach: build the full cross product of letters iteratively, one digit at a time, expanding a list of partial strings by appending every letter of the next digit's key to every existing partial string
bruteForce.time: O(4^n * n) where n is the number of digits (up to 4 letters per key)
bruteForce.space: O(4^n * n) for the intermediate lists
